Oh, and Derrick Henry will look to run all over his former team in the Tennessee Titans . That's a must-watch revenge game. Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Last week, we hit on Tee Higgins at +175 and tight end Harold Fannin Jr . at +235. Let's see what we have cooking up for Week 4. Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a tight end who looked incredible last week in his 2026 debut. Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook. 1. Raiders TE Brock Bowers (+160) The Las Vegas Raiders have a massive matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs this week. The Raiders are off to a surprising 3-0 start, although we can't ignore the fact that they've played the easiest strength of schedule in the NFL up to this point, as their first three opponents have won one game combined. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers made his season debut last week against the New Orleans Saints , and he looked magnificent. He caught a game-high 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown in a 35-27 win, and will be important if the Raiders want to score an upset victory over their rivals. With how good Bowers looked last week, I'll sprinkle on him again in this spot as Kirk Cousins ' new clear-cut "WR1." 2. Bills RB James Cook (-140) James Cook of the Buffalo Bills is one of the best running backs in the NFL, and he's on a bit of a heater right now. He rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 vs. the Detroit Lions , and then 24 times for 154 yards and another touchdown last week against the Los Angeles Chargers . Now, the flailing New England Patriots come to town, and they are missing two important defenders in Christian Barmore and Christian Gonzalez . They lost by 29 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars last week, and I'm sure Joe Brady and the Bills want to do something similar to the team that won their division last year. A -140 price isn't value, but I can tell you I was surprised by this listing. 3. Vikings RB Aaron Jones (-160) Like James Cook, this line doesn't offer much value. But consider that the Miami Dolphins have allowed six touchdowns to running backs through three games. The Minnesota Vikings are favored by double-digits over Miami, which makes sense because the Dolphins just lost De'Von Achane for the year, while Brian Flores is going to look to DESTROY his former team from a defensive standpoint. That means Aaron Jones is going to get plenty of touches. He hasn't scored since Week 1, but will in Week 4. 4. Jets RB Braelon Allen (+115) I was a fan of Braelon Allen in the 2024 draft process because he's big at 6-foot-1, 235 pounds, and was the youngest player in the entire class. He actually racked up 482 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns as a rookie, but an injury held him to four games played last year. Now, he's making his third career start with Breece Hall sidelined by a quad injury. When the New York Jets get in the red zone against the Chicago Bears , Frank Reich is going to call his number. 5. Saints RB Alvin Kamara (+135) (Monday) This game is on Monday night, but I had to mention it. The Saints are hosting the Atlanta Falcons in the 20th anniversary of the "Rebirth Game," where the Saints returned to the Superdome for the first time following Hurricane Katrina. The legendary Steve Gleason blocked a punt on the opening drive of the game, which set the tone for an emotional 23-3 Saints victory. I can't imagine what the environment will be like on Monday night. Travis Etienne is out with a hamstring injury, opening the door for franchise legend Alvin Kamara . He's not as productive as he used to be, but it makes too much sense for him to score in this game. Bonus: Ravens RB Derrick Henry 2 TDs (+250) Derrick Henry faces the team that selected him No. 45 overall in the 2016 NFL Draft this Sunday. Henry and the Titans didn't have some dramatic breakup, but Henry wanted to win football games and the Titans were about to suffer an embarrassing fall to the bottom of the league, so a mutual parting of ways made sense. It used to be a debate if Henry was a future Hall of Famer. Not anymore. The ageless wonder leads the NFL with 3,817 rushing yards and 38 rushing touchdowns since signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2024. Those are more rushing yards and more rushing touchdowns than the entire Titans offense since he left. Derrick Henry to find the end zone at -210 is probably a parlay leg, but what about two touchdowns at +250? He's averaging two touchdowns a game this year as it is! The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. Many of these fans place wagers on the teams they feel will win those head-to-head matchups. But the NFL is also built upon star power and athletic playmaking—with these exciting moments, come NFL player prop bets, allowing fans to place wagers on their favorite NFL players to perform like superstars. What Are NFL Player Props? NFL player prop bets allow fans to wager on the likelihood that a football star will perform above or below expectations in a specific statistical category, or that they will achieve certain notable events during the game. Like any wager, greater risk means higher payout, so placing a wager on a struggling quarterback to throw for four touchdowns will return stronger odds than a wager on the reigning MVP who has been on a hot streak. Why Bet on NFL Player Props? Player prop bets add a layer of entertainment to your NFL experience. Unlike a head-to-head matchup where you might place your bet and check the score after the game is over, placing wagers on individual achievements and statistics gives you even more reason to watch the game and root for the player you bet on. With a wager on a statistical category, each time that player achieves you are a step closer to a profitable bet, which adds entertainment and excitement to your experience. Just as there are a variety of positions, ways to score, and statistics involved in an NFL game, there are a wide variety of player prop bet options. Whether it is a wager on a favorite player or in a statistical category you love to follow, there is likely a player prop category for every bettor. Most Common NFL Player Prop Bets With so many unique positions and statistics in NFL football, there is just as much variety in the player prop bets available. You can choose over/under bets on passing yards, rushing yards, passing touchdowns, interceptions, and total receptions, depending on your chosen player’s position. If you notice that a receiver with potential is +500 to score a touchdown and you believe he’s due for a breakout game you will profit if the receiver scores a TD. You can also choose head-to-head matchups—for example, you can wager that your favorite quarterback will throw for more passing yards than the quarterback he is matched against in a given week. An NFL player prop is a bet on how an individual player will perform in a game. Instead of betting on the winner, point spread, or total score, you're betting on a specific outcome or statistic for that player. Common NFL player props include: Passing yards, completions, attempts, and passing touchdowns (quarterbacks). Rushing yards and rushing attempts (running backs, quarterbacks, and other rushers). Receptions and receiving yards (wide receivers, tight ends, and running backs). Anytime, first, and multiple touchdown scorers (eligible offensive players and defenses/special teams). Most player props are offered as over/under bets. For example, a sportsbook might set a quarterback's passing yards at 245.5. You can bet the over if you think he'll finish with 246 or more, or the under if you think he'll finish with 245 or fewer. Touchdown scorer props work differently: you’re simply betting whether a player scores, with the odds reflecting the sportsbook's assessment of how likely that is. One thing that makes player props different from game bets is how much they depend on the game script. A team that falls behind by three scores is likely to throw more and run less, which can boost passing and receiving opportunities while cutting into rushing volume. That's why our projections account for the expected game script when estimating how a player is likely to perform. From projection to probability : We run simulations of the upcoming game to estimate how often a player finishes over or under the specific line being offered.
